sentences.text: This is second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

First bail application was allowed vide order dated 21.7.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.31571 of 2023 and the applicant was released on bail, however, due to violation of the bail condition no.4 the bail order was cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.

The applicant has been arrested on 6.3.2025 by Police Station- Aron, District Guna in connection with Crime No.28/2023, registered in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376 (2) (n), 376 (3) of IPC and section 5(1)/6 of POCSO Act.

Prosecution case, in brief, is that father of prosecutrix lodged a report with the police station with regard to missing of his daughter since 22/4/2023 and she without informing her family member had left the house.

Complainant and his family member searched for the girl but she was not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16805 2 MCRC-13179-2025 found and a suspicion was raised on the applicant who had taken his daughter somewhere.

Thereafter during investigation on the basis of the statement of the complainant as well as other witnesses allegations the applicant was roped in and thereafter was arrested.

sentences.text: It is submitted that earlier applicant was released on bail by this Court vide order dated 21.7.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.31571 of 2023, however, the Court stipulated a condition that the applicant shall not commit any offence during pendency of the trial, failing which, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
It is submitted that due to violation of bail condition no.4, his bail was automatically cancelled and thereafter arrest warrant was issued and applicant was arrested on 6.3.2025.
It is further argued that the entire prosecution story is false and fabricated because the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
has not made any allegation against the present applicant.

Prosecutrix in her statement specifically stated that she wanted to marry the present applicant and infact they had performed marriage in Arya Samaj Temple and now they were living as husband and wife.
He is permanent resident of District Guna (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
He is ready to abide by the terms and conditions as may be imposed.
With the aforesaid submissions, prayer for grant of bail is made out.
Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16805 3 MCRC-13179-2025

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations and looking to the fact that applicant was previously released on bail by this Court, coupled with the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pre- trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court.

This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicant:-
